solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Want to collect stuff about French scientist (7)

indicatorNotes.to collect: to collect something is to take it in, so the first word gathers the next inside itself
indicatorNotes.about: 'about' as in 'turn about' means facing the other way, so the word it follows is written backwards

blocks.note: to want is to lack; this is the outer word
to stuff is to ram, as in cramming a bag; turned round before it goes in

annotation.surface: Someone longs to gather up material about a French scientist, perhaps for a biography.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Want' reads as desire in the surface, but the wordplay needs its other sense of shortage. 'Stuff' likewise looks like a noun, material, and works as the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Jean-Baptiste Lamarck was a French naturalist famous for an early theory of evolution, so he is a French scientist by example.

entries.clue: Supplication in Latin surprisingly unknown (6)

indicatorNotes.surprisingly: something that happens surprisingly does not go as expected, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

blocks.note: in algebra the unknowns are x, y and z

annotation.surface: A prayer turns out, to everyone's surprise, to be in Latin nobody knows.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface ties the prayer to Latin, which suits church liturgy, so the word feels like description rather than raw letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A litany is a set of petitions recited in church, a form of supplication: a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Second foolish person to accept female’s common sense (6,3)

indicatorNotes.to accept: to accept something is to take it in, so the fool's word takes the female's inside itself

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second, as in 'half a mo'
a twit is a fool; this word opens up to hold the next
the female's thing is hers; the 's also lets the phrase read as 'female is'

annotation.surface: In a second, a fool comes round to a woman's plain good sense.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like an ordinal or a verb meaning support, but it is the brief moment. The fool is split after its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Mother wit is native intelligence, the plain common sense someone is born with; a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Salad ingredient helping entertaining politician to lose weight finally (7)

indicatorNotes.entertaining: a host entertaining a guest has them inside the house, so the portion word holds the politician
indicatorNotes.to lose: to lose something is to be left without it, so this letter is taken out
indicatorNotes.finally: finally means at the end, so only the last letter of weight is used

blocks.note: a helping is a ration or portion
last letter of weight; this is the letter removed

annotation.surface: A politician is served a salad while trying to shed some pounds.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a diet, with 'lose weight' reading as one phrase; in fact 'weight' gives up only its last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Rampion is a bellflower whose roots and leaves were once eaten in salads, so it is a salad ingredient by example.

entries.clue: Member of ethnic group taking road to south of revolutionary country (4)

indicatorNotes.to south of: south is below on a map, and in a down entry below means after, so the road follows the country
indicatorNotes.revolutionary: a revolution is a turn, so the country's letters are turned round

blocks.note: the United Kingdom's abbreviation, turned round

annotation.surface: An emigrant takes the road south from a country in revolution.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests politics, but it only turns the country round. The country is the UK, not any land in revolt.
annotation.definitionFit: The Kurds are an ethnic group of the Middle East, so a Kurd is one member of that group.

entries.clue: Spooner’s able Christian correspondent concealed hazard (7)

indicatorNotes.Spooner’s: Rev. William Spooner was famous for swapping the first sounds of words, so this asks for that swap

blocks.note: St Paul wrote letters (epistles) to the early churches
swap the opening F and P sounds of the two words

annotation.surface: A capable Christian letter-writer hides a danger.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'correspondent' is not a journalist but St Paul, author of many New Testament letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A pitfall was originally a covered pit dug as a trap, so it is literally a hazard kept hidden.

entries.clue: Chum is in Paris protecting naughty kids — there’s something here that’s been covered up (10)

annotation.definition: there’s something here that’s been covered up

indicatorNotes.protecting: to protect is to shield on every side, so the words around the kids enclose them

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous child

annotation.surface: A friend in Paris shields some badly behaved children, hinting at a cover-up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In Paris' is the signal to translate the word before it into French. The definition is a whole descriptive phrase rather than a single synonym.
annotation.definitionFit: A palimpsest is a manuscript scraped and written over, so earlier writing lies covered up beneath the new.

entries.clue: Musical effect from US band captured by old group standing up (7)

indicatorNotes.captured by: something captured is held inside, so the band sits within the other letters
indicatorNotes.standing up: in a down entry a word standing up reads from bottom to top, so it is reversed

blocks.note: O for old, as in OT for Old Testament
a lot is a group or batch

annotation.surface: A musical trick borrowed from an American band gets taken up by an old group.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'old group' sounds like a veteran band to match the US one, but it is two pieces, old and group, reversed together.
annotation.definitionFit: A tremolo is a rapid wavering of a note, a plain example of a musical effect.

entries.clue: Provide weapons for French and protective headgear (5)

annotation.surface: An order to equip the French with guns and helmets.
annotation.walkthrough: 'French and' asks for the French word for 'and', not for anything French being armed.
annotation.definitionFit: An armet is a closed helmet of the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, a specific kind of protective headgear.

entries.clue: “Very good” diamonds are cut, put in place — by me? (8)

annotation.definition: “Very good” diamonds are cut, put in place — by me?

indicatorNotes.cut: a cut word is shortened, so the final letter of 'are' is dropped
indicatorNotes.put in: to put something in is to insert it, so the pieces go inside the word for place

blocks.note: to place is to lay; this word wraps round the rest
pi, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good
the word 'are' without its last letter

annotation.surface: A gem-cutter watches good diamonds being cut and set, and wonders whether it was their own work.
annotation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the answer: a craftsman cutting and setting diamonds asks 'by me?' The same words, read as parts, build it.
annotation.definitionFit: A lapidary is a craftsman who cuts, polishes and sets gemstones, so the whole clue reads straight as his job.

entries.clue: Convey source of magic is something symbolic (5)

indicatorNotes.source of: a source is where something starts, so only the first letter of magic is used

annotation.surface: A statement that a charm's power lies in what it stands for.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Convey' suggests communicating meaning, which fits the symbolic surface, but here it means carry.
annotation.definitionFit: A totem is an object or emblem that stands for a clan or spirit, so a plain synonym for something symbolic.

entries.clue: Help old lady beginning to promote proud plan? (6,3)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the P of promote is used

blocks.note: help given to those in need
one's old lady is one's mother

annotation.surface: Someone helps an elderly woman get a scheme she is proud of off the ground.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Proud' here means standing out from a surface, as raised features stand proud on a map; the question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: A relief map models hills as raised shapes, so it is a plan whose features stand proud: a punning definition.

entries.clue: More than one refusal is making use of reasoning abilities (6)

annotation.surface: Saying no again and again counts as thinking for yourself.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like a link to the definition but supplies the last two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Noesis is the working of the intellect, understanding reached by thought: a philosopher's word for the definition's activity.

entries.clue: Sent back superfluous note brought in from elsewhere (8)

indicatorNotes.Sent back: something sent back returns the way it came, so the letters are written in reverse

blocks.note: de trop, French borrowing for too much, unwanted
the third note of the sol-fa scale

annotation.surface: A needless memo is returned, having come in from another office.
annotation.walkthrough: The reversal covers both pieces together, so the note ends up first. De trop is a French phrase used in English for unwanted or excessive.
annotation.definitionFit: Imported goods are brought in from another country, a plain synonym.

entries.clue: A hotel confused with empty pub is welcoming (10)

indicatorNotes.confused: something confused is muddled up, so its letters are jumbled
indicatorNotes.empty: an empty word has lost its contents, so only its outside letters remain

annotation.surface: A muddled hotel paired with a deserted pub still gives visitors a warm reception.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like a link before the definition, but its letters are needed in the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: Hospitable means warmly receptive to guests, a plain synonym for welcoming.

entries.clue: One with lustful eyes now worshipped criminal (6-7)

indicatorNotes.criminal: a criminal act is a wrong one, so the letters are put in the wrong order

annotation.surface: A leering figure is now, absurdly, venerated as a criminal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lustful eyes' suggests a lecher, but the longing is only for goods behind shop glass.
annotation.definitionFit: A window-shopper gazes longingly at displays without buying: a playful definition by lust for goods.

entries.clue: End of day and mother’s hugged by father who dishes out cash? (9)

annotation.definitionNote: 'who dishes out cash' stands for 'one who dishes out cash', a noun

indicatorNotes.End of: the end of a word is its last letter, so only the Y of day is used
indicatorNotes.hugged by: something hugged is held in someone's arms, so these pieces sit inside the father

blocks.note: Latin for father, old public-school slang; wraps round the rest

annotation.surface: At the end of the day, Dad, not Mum, is the one handing over the money.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'father' the cash-giver, but he only supplies the outer letters; the definition starts at 'who'.
annotation.definitionFit: A paymaster is the official who pays out wages, so the definition describes his job.

entries.clue: Was weepy, in want of a father ultimately, like the prodigal son (8)

indicatorNotes.in want of: to be in want of something is to lack it, so these letters are missing
indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of father is taken

annotation.surface: The prodigal son, missing his father, was in tears.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface borrows the parable, where the son comes home in tears to his father; 'was' is kept as a word of the answer, not a link.
annotation.definitionFit: In the parable the prodigal son squandered his inheritance, so the Bible story is the example of wasteful.

entries.clue: Educational approach that could provide a posh trophy? No (13)

indicatorNotes.could provide: the fodder could supply the answer, given a rearrangement, so the letters are to be reordered

blocks.note: anagram fodder, tucked after the question mark

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether a teaching method could win a smart prize, and answers themselves: no.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No' looks like a comment on the question but belongs in the fodder. The answer is Rudolf Steiner's philosophy, the basis of Steiner schools.
annotation.definitionFit: Anthroposophy underpins Steiner-Waldorf education, so it serves as an educational approach by example.

entries.clue: Four in small American state are put up in holiday destination? (7)

indicatorNotes.in: one thing in another sits inside it, so the numeral goes into the state
indicatorNotes.put up: in a down entry, a word put up reads from the bottom, so it is reversed

blocks.note: Rhode Island, the smallest US state, abbreviated RI

annotation.surface: Four people from a tiny American state are put up at a resort.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Small' points to Rhode Island, the smallest state. 'Put up' reads as lodging, which suits the holiday, but it reverses.
annotation.definitionFit: The Riviera, the Mediterranean coast of France and Italy, is a holiday destination by example, hence the question mark.

entries.clue: Richard in fit of temper — one supporting wicked thing? (7)

indicatorNotes.in: one word in another sits inside it, so the name goes into the tantrum

blocks.note: to be in a pet is to be sulking

annotation.surface: Richard throws a tantrum, while someone else stands up for a villain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wicked thing' is not a villain but something with a wick: a candle.
annotation.definitionFit: A pricket is a spike on which a candle is stuck, so it supports a thing with a wick.

entries.clue: Summoner to service finished early outside the place of worship (6)

indicatorNotes.finished early: something finished early stops short of its end, so the word loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.outside: the shortened word goes on the outside, wrapping round 'the'

blocks.note: a church bell calls people to service

annotation.surface: A church bell rang short before the service at the chapel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests waiting at table or the army, but it is a church service. The name is Hebrew for 'house of God'.
annotation.definitionFit: A bethel is a chapel, especially a Nonconformist one, so a plain synonym for place of worship.

entries.clue: Pretty monkey, very small, had food (8)

blocks.note: v is the standard abbreviation of very, the small version of the word

annotation.surface: A cute, tiny monkey has just eaten.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' is the verb, as in 'pretty up', not an adjective describing the monkey.
annotation.definitionFit: To titivate is to smarten or make prettier, matching the verb 'to pretty'.

entries.clue: Old character conflicted about leader of house (5)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so the word for conflicted goes round the letter
indicatorNotes.leader of: the leader goes first, so only the first letter of house is used

annotation.surface: An aged person is torn about a house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Character' means a letter of an alphabet, not a person.
annotation.definitionFit: Thorn (þ) is an Old English letter for the 'th' sound, now dropped, so an old character in the alphabet sense.

entries.clue: Countenance opposing one person deemed wise (6)

blocks.note: a sage is a wise person

annotation.surface: Someone opposes a single wise elder.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Countenance' could be the verb 'tolerate', which would sit well beside 'opposing'; it is the noun meaning face.
annotation.definitionFit: Countenance and visage are both literary nouns for a person's face.

entries.clue: One short idiot who is obsessively revered? (4)

annotation.definitionNote: 'who is obsessively revered' stands for 'one who is', a noun

indicatorNotes.short: a word that is short is missing something, so the idiot loses its last letter

blocks.note: a dolt is a stupid person

annotation.surface: A slightly dim person finds themselves worshipped by fans.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One short idiot' reads as a single insult, but 'one' is a numeral and 'short' trims the idiot.
annotation.definitionFit: An idol is someone adored to excess, a figure worshipped like a god.

entries.clue: Part of garden inferior — beginning to blossom, given nutrition all around (9)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the B of blossom is used
indicatorNotes.all around: something all around encircles the rest, so the word for given nutrition goes on the outside

blocks.note: fed; this word wraps round the rest

annotation.surface: A poor patch of garden only starts to bloom once it has been fed all over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blossom' suits the garden but gives only one letter; the flower in the answer comes from 'inferior'.
annotation.definitionFit: A flowerbed is a planted plot, one part of a garden: a definition by what it belongs to.

entries.clue: Vessel in plan, the first to “set sail” (5)

indicatorNotes.the first to: the first of a word is its first letter, so only the S of 'set' is meant
indicatorNotes.set sail: a ship that sets sail departs, so that letter leaves the word for plan

blocks.note: a sketch is a rough plan
first letter of set, which is removed

annotation.surface: A boat drawn in a plan is the first to get under way.
annotation.walkthrough: The quotation marks show 'set sail' doing a double job: 'set' supplies the letter, and 'set sail' tells it to leave.
annotation.definitionFit: A ketch is a two-masted sailing boat, a vessel by example.

entries.clue: What could indicate eagle making descent? (7)

blocks.note: the answer, split into parts, reads as an instruction to insert one letter into four others, and following it spells the bird
the definition, in the sense of ancestry rather than a dive

annotation.surface: A question about an eagle swooping down.
annotation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer is the wordplay and the clue is its result. LINEAGE split as L IN EAGE says put L inside EAGE, giving EAGLE.
annotation.definitionFit: Lineage is ancestry, one's line of descent: a plain synonym in the family sense.

entries.clue: Actual / error that could make dad mad (7)

annotation.definition2: error that could make dad mad

blocks.note: first sense: exact, taken word for word

blocks.clueFragment: error that could make dad mad
blocks.note: second sense: printers' slang for a typo, such as one wrong letter changing dad to mad

annotation.surface: A slip that would drive a father round the bend.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mad' reads as angry, but the error is a one-letter misprint that turns the word dad into mad.
annotation.definitionFit: Literal as an adjective means actual or exact; as a noun it is a misprint.
